items.title: Oil prices stoke inflation while weak jobs undercut the hike case — gold wins on both sides

items.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent: the Strait of Hormuz will 'become irrelevant'
items.summary: CLS, August 8 — In an interview with NBC on August 6, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the Strait of Hormuz will never return to what it was. He stressed this is not the Iran-favourable situation Tehran has portrayed, but rather that the strait will lose its current status as a chokepoint for energy transport.

items.summary: CLS, August 8 — The latest forecast has Typhoon Baihaitun making landfall along the coast between Zhoushan in Zhejiang and Fuding in Fujian between the night of the 9th and the morning of the 10th. Wind and rain across east China will be concentrated from the 8th to the 12th, with the rainfall timetable showing the specific window for each area.

items.title: 116,000 new companies were established in humanoid robotics in the first half of this year
items.summary: CLS, August 8 — Data from the State Administration for Market Regulation show that companies in new industries and new tracks kept building momentum in the first half of 2026, with 116,000 new firms established in humanoid robotics, up 9.5% year on year. Services-related business entities were a highlight, manufacturing firms accelerated their transformation, and the industry showed numerous bright spots.

items.title: Ukraine says Kyiv and other areas came under attack, with several killed and wounded
items.summary: CLS, August 8 — Kyiv's city military administration reported on the 8th that the city was attacked by Russian forces in the early hours; as of 05:45 local time the attack had injured four people and started fires in two districts of Kyiv, with rescue operations under way.

items.title: China approves its first drug for the prevention of acute mountain sickness
items.summary: CLS, August 8 — Following strict review and approval by the National Medical Products Administration, acetazolamide sustained-release capsules have been approved for market. With Professor Gesang Luobu, deputy head of the People's Hospital of Tibet Autonomous Region and director of the Tibet Institute of High Altitude Medicine, as principal investigator, it becomes the first drug approved in China with an indication for preventing acute mountain sickness.
